dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: هلا، عندي حجز على اسم نور
dialogue.english: Hello, I have a reservation under the name Nour.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Welcome, one moment let me check.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: إي، غرفة لشخصين لثلاث ليالي، صح؟
dialogue.transliteration: ee, ghurfa la-shakhSeen la-thalaath layaali, Sa7?
dialogue.english: Yes, a room for two for three nights, right?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: إي صح، الفطور مشمول ويا الغرفة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ee Sa7, il-fi6oor mashmool wiyya l-ghurfa?
dialogue.english: Yes right, is breakfast included with the room?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Yes, from seven to ten in the restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: Can I see the room first?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Of course, this is your room on the third floor.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: Where's the elevator please?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: In front of you on the right.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: What time do I need to check out?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: At twelve noon.

response.arabic: إي اكو، غرفة لشخصين بالطابگ الثالث
response.transliteration: ee aku, ghurfa la-shakhSeen bi6-6aabag ith-thaalith
response.english: Yes there is, a room for two on the third floor.

pair.english: How much is the price per night?
Is breakfast included with the room?
What time do I need to check out?

lessons.culture: In Iraqi hotels the clerk usually welcomes you with 'hala beek' and offers tea while the papers are done. Prices are often quoted in dinars, and asking to see the room first is normal and not rude.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: السلام عليكم، اريد احجز تذكرة باص للبصرة
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum, areed a7jiz tathkira baas lil-basra
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, I want to book a bus ticket to Basra.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: وعليكم السلام، ذهاب بس لو ذهاب وإياب؟
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykum is-salaam, thihaab bass low thihaab w iyaab?
dialogue.english: And upon you peace, one-way or round trip?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: Round trip, how much is the price?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Thirty thousand dinars.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: Is there a discount for students?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Yes, as long as you bring your university ID.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: What time does the next bus leave?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.transliteration: is-saa3a tis3a, w aku karaasi faargha
dialogue.english: At nine, and there are free seats.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: Can I pay by card?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: No, cash only.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Here you go, here's your ticket, have a good trip.

pair.english: Do you have tickets to Basra?
What time does the bus leave?

response.english: At nine from the bus station.

pair.english: How long does the trip take?

lessons.culture: Intercity buses in Iraq leave from the karaaj (bus station), and many counters still take cash in dinars only, so ask before counting on a card. Students often get a discount if they show a university ID.

dialogue.english: Excuse me, where's the check-in counter?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Straight ahead, after the second door.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Your passport and ticket please.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.transliteration: tfaDDal, haay jawaazi w haay tathkirti
dialogue.english: Here you go, here's my passport and my ticket.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: How many bags can I take?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: شنطتين، ووزن كل وحدة عشرين كيلو
dialogue.transliteration: shan6iteen, w wazin kull wa7da 3ishreen keelo
dialogue.english: Two bags, and each one weighs twenty kilos.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: Where's the plane gate?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: بوابة خمسة، والطيارة تگلع الساعة ستة
dialogue.transliteration: bawwaaba khamsa, w i6-6ayyaara tigla3 is-saa3a sitta
dialogue.english: Gate five, and the plane departs at six.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Do you have anything to declare?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: No, I don't have anything.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Welcome to Iraq, go ahead.

response.english: Here you go, this is my passport.

pair.english: Are you coming for tourism or work?
How long will you stay here?
Do you have anything to declare?

lessons.culture: Officers at Baghdad airport are usually brisk but polite, and 'hala beek bil-3iraag' is a genuine welcome, often followed by a question about why you came. Answering plainly with 'siyaa7a' or 'shughul' is enough.

phrases.arabic: الله يعوّض، ان شاء الله تنحل
phrases.transliteration: allah y3awwiD, in shaa2 allah tin7all

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: لو سمحت، تعال ساعدني، ضيّعت شنطتي
dialogue.transliteration: law sama7t, ta3aal saa3idni, Dayya3it shan6ti
dialogue.english: Excuse me, come help me, I lost my bag.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: I'm coming now, what does the bag look like?

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.transliteration: sooda w kabeera, w inkisrat il-3ajala maalatha
dialogue.english: Black and big, and its wheel got broken.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: لا تخاف، راح نلگاها ان شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: laa tkhaaf, raa7 nilgaaha in shaa2 allah
dialogue.english: Don't worry, we'll find it God willing.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: والطيارة متأخرة هواية، وفاتتني الرحلة الثانية
dialogue.transliteration: w i6-6ayyaara mit2akhkhra hawaaya, w faatatni ir-ri7la ith-thaanya
dialogue.english: And the plane is very delayed, and I missed the other flight.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.english: What do I do? I need to change the flight.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Go to the complaints office, they'll help you there.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: روحت وما لگيت أحد، محد رد عليّ
dialogue.transliteration: ruu7it w ma lageet a7ad, ma7ad radd 3alayya
dialogue.english: I went and didn't find anyone, nobody answered me.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.english: Wait a little, I'll call them now.

dialogue.speaker: نور
dialogue.arabic: الله يعوّض، ان شاء الله تنحل، شكراً
dialogue.transliteration: allah y3awwiD, in shaa2 allah tin7all, shukran
dialogue.english: May God make up for it, God willing it'll work out, thanks.

pair.english: What do I do? I missed the plane.

response.english: Don't worry, we'll change the flight.
After the door, on the left.
Wait a little, I'll call them now.

lessons.culture: When something goes wrong, Iraqis say 'allah kareem' (God is generous) or 'in shaa2 allah tin7all' to stay calm and hopeful, and staff will often say 'laa tkhaaf' (don't worry). Speaking politely with 'law sama7t' gets help faster than raising your voice.

challenge.title: Book a Trip and Handle a Problem
challenge.instructions: اكتب حوار قصير: احجز غرفة بفندق او تذكرة سفر، وبعدين صارت مشكلة (تأخير، شنطة ضايعة، او فاتتك الرحلة) وگول شلون حليتها.
required_elements: طلب حجز او تذكرة بجملة كاملة

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: هلا، اريد احجز تذكرة باص للبصرة
dialogue.transliteration: hala, areed a7jiz tathkira baas lil-basra
dialogue.english: Hello, I want to book a bus ticket to Basra.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.transliteration: thihaab bass low thihaab w iyaab?
dialogue.english: One-way or round trip?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Round trip, how much is the price?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: ثلاثين ألف دينار، والباص يطلع الساعة تسعة
dialogue.transliteration: thalaatheen alif deenaar, w il-baas y6la3 is-saa3a tis3a
dialogue.english: Thirty thousand dinars, and the bus leaves at nine.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: للأسف فاتني الباص، اكو باص ثاني؟
dialogue.transliteration: lil-asaf faatni l-baas, aku baas thaani?
dialogue.english: Unfortunately I missed the bus, is there another one?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: لا تخاف، اكو باص بعد ساعتين
dialogue.transliteration: laa tkhaaf, aku baas ba3d saa3teen
dialogue.english: Don't worry, there's a bus in two hours.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: May God make up for it, thanks a lot.
